citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. III 'The Rate of Growth', section 'Regeneration, or growth and repair', pp. 138-149, Figs. 35-40 (claim registry cites pp. 50-155, Figs. 33-40)
claim: Regeneration restores form at a measurable rate related to the amount removed (Durbin/Ellis tail-regeneration curves), i.e. restoration of form is itself a lawful growth process.

formalism.name: Regenerative growth curves: velocity decay law (Durbin) and amount-removed scaling / isochrones (Ellis)

state_variables.L(t): cumulative regenerated tail length (mm) at t days after amputation
state_variables.R: amount of tail removed (mm, or per cent of tail length)
state_variables.p_n(R): fraction of the removed amount restored after n days
state_variables.t_q(R): time (days) to restore q per cent of the removed amount (Thompson Fig. 40 isochrones)

equations.E1_velocity_is_derivative: V(t) = dL/dt; Thompson p. 141-142: Fig. 36 (V vs t) is 'the first derivative' of Fig. 35 (L vs t)
equations.E2_thompson_power_decay: V * t^n = const with n ~ 2 ('the velocity varies, or tends to vary, inversely as the square of the time', p. 143); integrated: L(t) = L_inf - c / t
equations.E3_log_linear_decay: log V falls 'approximately into a straight line' against t (Fig. 37, p. 142): V = V0 exp(-k t); integrated monomolecular / von Bertalanffy-type approach L(t) = L_inf (1 - exp(-k (t - t0)))
equations.E4_sigmoid_with_inflection: For larger tadpoles (Exp. IV) V rises to a maximum 'about the seventh day' then falls (pp. 144-145); L(t) is sigmoid with an inflection at t_i = argmax V
equations.E5_amount_removed_scaling: Absolute amount regenerated after a fixed time increases with the amount removed; p_n(R) is nearly independent of R for small R, so L_n(R) = p_n(R) * R is approximately proportional to R (Ellis table p. 148)
equations.E6_isochrone_cubic_parabola: Fig. 40 isochrones t_q(R): t_q(0) = 0, t_q(R) -> infinity as R -> R_crit = 75 % of tail, and 'each curve approximates in form to a cubic parabola' (R ~ t^3, i.e. t_q ~ R^(1/3)) for the rising part
equations.E7_incomplete_restoration: 'regeneration tends to fall somewhat short of a complete restoration of the lost part' (p. 146): plateau p_inf(R) < 1 (Ellis: 0.44-0.48)

boundary_conditions.L(0): 0 (nothing regenerated at amputation); first measurement at t = 3 days so the 0-3 day latent period is unobserved (p. 139-140)
boundary_conditions.R_crit: 75 % of tail removed -> no regeneration, death (Ellis fifth series, p. 148)

parameter_regimes.thompson_claim: V t^2 ~ const; log V linear in t; no inflection observed after day 3
point of inflection about the seventh day; same 1/T^2 decline afterwards

parameter_regimes.organism: Rana clamitans tadpoles (Ellis 1909), ~40 mm body, ~26 mm tail
parameter_regimes.thompson_claim: amount regenerated related to amount removed; isochrones are cubic parabolas converging to infinity at 75 %
no regeneration, animal died (critical amputation level)

empirical_claims_tested.text: Regenerated length vs time is a smooth, lawful growth curve (Durbin Exp. II and IV).
empirical_claims_tested.test: goodness of fit (r, RMSE) of exponential-approach and hyperbolic (Thompson V t^2) laws to Thompson's printed tables

empirical_claims_tested.text: Velocity declines inversely as the square of time (V t^2 = const) after the first measurement.
empirical_claims_tested.test: log-log slope n of daily increment vs time on Thompson's interpolated table; compare n to 2 and to exponential alternative

empirical_claims_tested.text: Larger tadpoles (Exp. IV) show a point of inflection about day 7.
empirical_claims_tested.test: argmax of Thompson's interpolated daily increments and inflection of fitted logistic/Gompertz curves

empirical_claims_tested.text: The amount regenerated in a given time is related to (increases with) the amount removed.
empirical_claims_tested.test: Pearson r and through-origin slope of mm regenerated (day 9, day 32 plateau) vs mm removed across Ellis series O, P, R, S

empirical_claims_tested.text: Time to restore q % of the removed amount grows with R like a cubic parabola and diverges at 75 %.
empirical_claims_tested.test: log-log slope of interpolated isochrone t_q(R) vs R for q = 20, 30, 40 (expected ~1/3); fit t_q = a R^b / (75 - R)^c form

pre_scouted_dataset.match_reason: Single 60-day endpoint of tail regrowth (cm) for 10 autotomised lizards; amount removed is recorded only as YES/NO, no time series, no amputation-level gradient.
